mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions compressing growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: high inflation or policy tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30 months (p > 0.1) during the same policy regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coinciding with UNRATE below 5% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above previous month's value AND UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market strengthening before earnings season
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of more than 2% followed by a rebound in the next month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the reversal signals improving supply-side momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > -2% in month t AND HOUST rises in month t+1
failure_condition: No significant return advantage over 20 days (rank IC > 0.05) during similar production reversals.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% over three months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects growing output capacity and future earnings potential.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative and consistent across 10 such INDPRO expansion episodes (median p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a single month while FEDFUNDS remains below 3%, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 20-day forward return as inflation pressures outweigh rate easing benefits.
regime_hint: inflation surprise in a low-rate environment
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly different from the prior 12-month mean during similar inflation-rate spikes (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below 400 million dollars combined with a rising UNRATE above 6% in the prior month predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak retail demand and higher unemployment pressure valuations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 400 AND UNRATE crosses above 6% in the prior month
regime_hint: labor market tightening and weak retail demand
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during analogous labor and retail signals.

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of declining GDPC1 (GDP momentum) followed by a month of stable or modest growth predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a bottoming in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two months then holds or rises in the third
failure_condition: No significant forward return advantage over 20 days (rank IC > 0.05) in 5 such GDPC1 reversal episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, the S&P 500 is expected to show a positive 60-day forward return as lower unemployment supports stronger corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months AND inflation regime is low
regime_hint: labor market loosening in a deflationary context
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative or flat with no statistical significance (p > 0.1) across 4 such UNRATE easing episodes.
